name: Sturdy Gatherables Chest
trait: The one chest crafting and refinement read from
summary: At the Smithy, every Sturdy Gatherables Chest in your house counts as part of your bag: crafting and refinement read its materials without you carrying them. 1,000 slots a chest, 50 Silver at any furniture shop, and you can place several. Ore, timber, hides and herbs live here; food, outfits and quest items have chests of their own.

capacity.basis: 1,000 slots a chest, and more than one can be placed (1.04 notes; KeenGamer).

payoff.basis: Crafting and refinement read it in place (1.04 notes): the only chest the Smithy reads.

unlock.basis: 50 Silver at any furniture shop once the Chapter III house is open.

tips.text: Insects and fish don't stack: every one takes a slot. Keep the ones your recipes use and sell or donate the rest.
Retrieve All (1.04) packs every placed chest at once; The Games Wiki reports contents surviving a move, but marks it unconfirmed.

watch: No source lists what the chest refuses. The Games Wiki marks the 'whole Materials tab' rule unconfirmed, so cloth, reagents, insects and mushrooms show as Reported.
The 1.04 note doesn't say whether every Smithy reads the chest or only one near the house; one guide calls the link global, The Games Wiki marks it unconfirmed.
Whether the Cauldron (alchemy) or the Workstation reads it isn't documented: carry those materials.

patches.note: Added with 1,000 slots; crafting and refinement read it

sources.title: How to Unlock All Storage Spaces

name: Kuku Cooler
trait: The pantry cooking reads from
summary: Food storage that cooking reads in place: raw ingredients stay in the cooler while you cook. The quest cooler holds 40, the Enhanced cooler 330, and coolers stacked in the house reach 1,000. It also keeps meals, elixirs and horse feed, though a meal has to be in the bag to be eaten.

capacity.basis: 330 per Enhanced cooler and 1,000 once coolers are stacked (Vulkk); the quest cooler holds 40.

payoff.basis: Cooking reads it in place (1.04 notes).

unlock.basis: A Chapter IV quest for the first; the Enhanced cooler needs Mercury from Delesyia research after Chapter XI.

tips.text: A fish fills a slot on its own; a Fish Fillet stacks to 50. Game8 says cleaning a fish gives fillets.
Cooking in the field? Keep one stack each of meat, vegetables, fruit, grain, cooking oil, water, salt and eggs in the bag.

watch: Meals must be in the bag to be eaten; the cooler only keeps them.
Mushrooms were cooking ingredients until 1.16 made them alchemy materials; no source says whether the cooler still takes them.
Vulkk's guide gives the quest cooler 50 slots; the 1.04 notes, KeenGamer and Vulkk's own database say 40.

patches.note: Kuku Cooler (40) and Enhanced Kuku Cooler (330) added; cooking reads both

sources.title: How to Unlock All Storage Spaces

name: Private Storage
trait: The catch-all: nearly anything, up to 1,000 slots
summary: The one chest that takes nearly everything: gear, consumables, materials and trade goods, though not Key Items or quest items. It starts at 240 slots and grows with each camp expansion to 1,000. Nothing reads it in place, so a recipe won't see what's in here: move materials to the house chests that crafting and cooking read.

payoff.basis: Storage only: no mechanic reads it in place. Bag sorting carries over while it's open (Vulkk).

unlock.basis: There from Chapter I: a tent at the Freesword Encampment, then the Hernand lodgings, then Kliff's tent at camp.

tips.text: Chapters I and II: the chest is in the north-east tent of the Freesword Encampment outside Hernand Castle, and at the Hernand lodgings.
After the camp moves to Pailune you receive Private Storage as an item you can place in the house.
Keep unique boss and exploration gear here rather than selling it: it can't be had again.

watch: Key Items and quest items can't go in: the Collectibles Chest takes quest items.
The 1.04 notes promised Private Storage its own category tabs 'in the near future'; no later note confirms them.

patches.note: Added at the Hernand lodgings and the Howling Hill camp
Moved into Kliff's tent at camp
A placeable Private Storage after the camp moves to Pailune

name: Wardrobe
trait: Outfits for all three, worn from the housing screen
summary: Each Wardrobe holds 100 outfits and armour pieces in one pool that Kliff, Damiane and Oongka share, and you can dress straight from the housing screen. Place up to ten for 1,000 slots. They cost 15 Silver at the Timberton furniture shop in Delesyia.

capacity.basis: 100 a wardrobe, 1,000 with ten placed (1.04 notes).

payoff.basis: Outfits are worn from the housing screen without taking them out, and all three characters share them (KeenGamer).

unlock.basis: Delesyia's Timberton furniture shop, or the camp shop after 100 Trust and a contract.

requires: A house to place it in (the Hernand Residence opens in Chapter III)

steps: Buy a Large Dark or Large Bright Timberton Wardrobe for 15 Silver from the furniture shop in Timberton, Delesyia.
Or raise the Delesyia furniture vendor to 100 Trust with Copper Pouches and buy the Contract: Wardrobes then sell at the Greymane Camp furniture shop.
Place up to ten in Build Mode; dress from the housing screen.

location: Timberton furniture shop, Delesyia; the Greymane Camp furniture shop after the contract.

name: Collectibles Chest
kind: House chest · quest items and recipes
trait: Where quest items, keys and recipes go
summary: 1,000 slots for the paper that clogs the bag: quest items, keys, notes, bounty posters, blueprints, recipes and books. Private Storage refuses quest items, so this is the one chest that takes them. It's a free reward from Early Encounter.

payoff.basis: Takes the quest items Private Storage refuses (The Games Wiki; KeenGamer).

unlock.basis: Early Encounter in Hernand Requests; House Roberts' quests may need to come first.

requires: A house to place it in

steps: Take Early Encounter from Hernand Requests (A Friendly Encounter); if no marker shows, progress House Roberts' faction quests.
Speak with the servant at the Timberturner Wainwright, north of the Nas River.
At the Timberham Sawmill the Noble gives you the chest; it appears under the Furniture tab.
Place it in Build Mode.

tips.text: Sell a recipe once you've read it: it's learned, and it sells for about half what it cost.
Discard old quest papers once they stop being Key Items; they sell for little.

watch: No source says whether a quest reads items from the chest: carry what a quest asks for.

name: Kuku Pot
trait: Seals world objects for Kuku crafting
summary: Not the cooler: the Kuku Pot is a carried store of 230 slots for what you lift with Axiom Force. That means Abyss objects, machine parts and contraptions, plus Aeserion's Scales and Abyss Cells. Grimnir's Kuku recipes use what's sealed inside. Every pot shares one pool, so a second pot adds no room.

capacity.basis: 230 slots, one pool for every pot (method.gg; The Games Wiki).

payoff.basis: Kuku crafting reads it, and it is the only way to carry a world object somewhere else.

unlock.basis: The Chapter IV main quest, Mysterious Pot.

steps: Finish Mysterious Pot in Chapter IV: Grimnir at the Kilnden Workshop makes you the Kuku Pot.
To seal: hold Axiom Force on an object marked by a small white swirl rune on the minimap and choose Seal.
Discard puts an object back into the world; Take Out moves Scales and Cells into the bag.
Lost it? Carl's Recover Items tab returns it (1.11), or Grimnir crafts another from 5 Iron Ore and 5 Timber.

location: Carried; crafted and upgraded at the Kilnden Workshop, Hernand.

tips.text: Making a Small Kuku A.T.A.G. (the part for Blackstar's armour) uses the whole pot: empty it first.

watch: Kuku-upgraded gear no longer counts toward its base item's challenges: finish those first or keep a spare.
Some objects hurt when they drop out of the pot: Discard in open ground.

patches.note: Carl's Recover Items tab returns a lost Kuku Pot

name: Camp Provisions
trait: The stock every mission and ship build draws on
summary: Carl's Camp Provisions is a stockpile, not a chest. What you donate becomes five camp resources: Armaments, Stone, Timber, Food and Silver. Missions, camp expansions and shipbuilding spend them, and none of them read your bag or your chests. Donations are one-way. Small Shipbuilding alone takes 600 Stone, 600 Wood and 1,200 Food from here.

capacity.basis: A stockpile with no published limit.

payoff.basis: Every dispatch, expansion and ship build draws on it (KeenGamer; Whisper of the House's shipbuilding panel).

unlock.basis: Carl opens donations after the Reed Devil fight in Chapter III (All Things How).

requires: Chapter III: the Greymane Camp, after the Reed Devil

steps: Talk to Carl at the Greymane Camp and choose Camp Provisions.
Pick items with the donation mark, or Donate Funds for Copper and Silver.
Feed the resource your queued missions use: Logging, Mining and Harvest burn Silver and Food fastest; later expansions run short of Armaments.

location: Carl, the Provisions Keeper, at the Greymane Camp.

slots.unit: resources: Armaments · Stone · Timber · Food · Silver

tips.text: As the camp ranks up, donated supplies turn up around the camp as food, weapons and supplies you can pick up again.

watch: Donations are permanent.
Guides name the five differently: KeenGamer's Armaments, Stone, Timber, Food and Silver; All Things How's Equipment, Ore, Lumber, Food and Coin.

name: Supply Chest
trait: Missed loot lands here, until it's full
summary: You can't put anything in Carl's Supply Chest. Missed loot, stronghold and clearing rewards, mission loot and camp produce land in it by themselves. It holds 230 slots and stops collecting when it's full, so empty it whenever you pass.

payoff.basis: Catches loot you would otherwise lose; you still carry it out yourself.

unlock.basis: The Chapter III camp; before that, a chest inside the Royal Trading Post in Hernand City.

steps: Speak with Carl at the Greymane Camp and open the Supply Chest.
Take everything out: sort it into the house chests, or donate it to Camp Provisions.
Before Chapter III the early chest stands inside the Royal Trading Post in Hernand City.

location: Behind Carl at the Greymane Camp; earlier, inside the Royal Trading Post in Hernand City.

tips.text: Mission loot and what the camp produces land here; much of it feeds crafting and cooking.

watch: When it's full it stops collecting: anything that would have landed there is lost.

name: Ship Holds
area: Fleetmasters at Vellua, Demeniss and Delesyia
trait: 6 to 36 slots of sea trade goods
summary: A ship's hold carries trade goods and nothing else: 6 slots on a rowboat, 14 on a small hull, 22 on a medium and 36 on a large one. A slot stacks 10 or 100 packed goods by price. No source publishes the legendary ships' holds.

capacity.basis: 36 slots at most on a bought hull (the Buy Ship screen, Whisper of the House).

payoff.basis: Maritime trading runs through it (KeenGamer).

unlock.basis: The DLC and a hull of your own: 2,000 to 6,000,000 Camp Funds.

requires: Charting the Unknown: A Wider World

steps: At a Fleetmaster (Hopkins at Vellua; Demeniss; Delesyia) the Buy Ship screen shows each hull's Inventory.
Load trade goods at a port; the hold takes nothing else.
Crew Carpenters so the hull repairs at sea; a lost ship is recovered at a Ship Manager for a fee.

location: Fleetmasters at Vellua, Demeniss and Delesyia.

figures.label: Repair and retrieval, one case at Vellua

name: Shipbuilding Stock
trait: Fill Carl's stock before the ship dispatch
summary: Small Shipbuilding is a dispatch, and its materials come out of Camp Provisions, not your bag: 600 Stone, 600 Wood and 1,200 Food, plus 10,000 Camp Funds. It also wants five free comrades, one of them an engineer, and 12 in-game hours. The Medium and Large builds take far more stock and add ocean materials. Donate ore, timber and food to Carl before you start.

payoff.basis: Your first ship, for less in Camp Funds than any you can buy.

unlock.basis: The DLC's A Wider World, after the camp expansion quests.

payoff.basis: Sails add +100 Health and +1 or +2 Speed; a figurehead +400 Health (Gaming Deputy).

name: Sea Blueprints
area: Ocula · Iliya · the Great Coral Reef · Port Delesyia
trait: Four ship parts no outfitter sells
summary: The best ship parts aren't for sale. The Giant Golden Compass Sail's manual is in a chest behind a waterfall at Castaway's Shelter on Ocula Island. The Steam and Clockwork Stern and Figurehead share a chest in sunken ruins west of Iliya Island. The Bluewake Sail lies in a cave deep in the Great Coral Reef, and the Long-Horned Fish Stern costs 50 Relics from Rafi at Port Delesyia.

payoff.basis: +200 Health and +2 Speed on the Compass Sail; the sterns push a ship against the wind (Gaming Deputy; FinalBoss).

unlock.basis: DLC exploration, deep dives and a 50-Relic purchase at Trust 100.

requires: A ship and a diving suit (Charting the Unknown)

routes.label: Giant Golden Compass Sail
steps: Sail to Ocula Island and find Castaway's Shelter, as the in-game banner names it.
Go behind the waterfall: the chest at the back holds the manual.
Read it, then craft it at a Workstation: 1 Natural Pearl, 30 Shiny Ore, 1 Giant Hydrothermal Salamander, 200 Flawless Timber, 90 Fleece.

routes.label: Steam and Clockwork Stern and Figurehead
steps: From Iliya Island, south of Hernand, head about 400 m west of its westernmost rocky landmass to the Forgotten Ocean Ruins.
Dive to the sunken temple, deal with the Abyss turret sentries and go in.
Look up and swim through the holes in the ceiling to the upper chamber: one chest holds both blueprints.

routes.label: Long-Horned Fish Stern
steps: Raise Trust with Rafi, the Relic Exchange vendor at Delesyia's port, to 100 by gifting money bags from floating salvage crates.
Buy the blueprint for 50 Relics; giant hydrothermal salamanders drop 1 to 3 each.
It fits large hulls only.

routes.label: Bluewake Sail
steps: Dive to the cave deep in the Great Coral Reef where Shiny Ore grows thick.
The treasure chest there holds the blueprint.

location: Castaway's Shelter, Ocula Island; the Forgotten Ocean Ruins west of Iliya Island; the Great Coral Reef; Port Delesyia.

tips.text: Craft at a Workstation (the Timberham Sawmill has one, through facility management), then fit the part at a Ship Manager.

name: Ocean Materials
trait: Where the sea's materials come from
summary: Charting the Unknown's parts run on materials found only at sea. Shiny Ore glows pale blue on the ocean floor and fills drifting boxes. Hydrothermal Mineral Deposits line the vent walls, and square salvage crates drop Ambergris and money bags. Natural Pearls come from the Iliya Ruins Excavation dispatch, Manganese from chests in sunken ships.

payoff.basis: Ship parts, sails and the DLC's gear need them.

unlock.basis: The DLC: a ship and a diving suit to reach them.

requires: A ship and a diving suit (Charting the Unknown)

steps: Sail with the ship's underwater detection on, and break every square salvage crate you pass.
Dive to the pale blue Shiny Ore nodes; an upgraded mining tool gets more from each.
Break Hydrothermal Mineral Deposits on the vent walls with Force Palm or a mining drill.
Pioneer Iliya Island and run its Ruins Excavation dispatch for Natural Pearls.

location: The ocean floor, the Great Hydrothermal Vents, the Great Coral Reef, sunken ships and floating salvage.

name: Ship Teleportation Device
trait: Turns your ship into a fast-travel point
summary: Fitted, it makes the ship a fast-travel destination, so its hold and crew wait where you left them. The blueprint is buried on Auronui's west coast. It costs 15 Shiny Ore, 5 Azurite and 10 Iron Ore at the camp's furniture workbench.

payoff.basis: The ship becomes a fast-travel point (KeenGamer).

unlock.basis: Auronui's pioneering mission and a buried chest; the materials are common.

name: Island Storage
area: Built on an island you pioneer
trait: Island produce and rough-quest loot, kept on the island
summary: An island building that stores loot from rough quests and missions and the supplies your islands produce, as its in-game text puts it (Vulkk records it). The listing names Logging 2, Weaving 4 and Crafting 4. No source publishes its size or how you open it.

payoff.basis: Item text only: storage for island produce and quest loot.

unlock.basis: The DLC: pioneer an island first (three comrades, a 12-hour dispatch on Auronui).

name: Horse Trade Slots
trait: One slot of trade goods; two on Elantrima and Rokade
summary: A horse carries trade goods and nothing else: one slot on most horses, two on Elantrima and Rokade. Since 1.16 a slot stacks 10 or 100 packed goods by price, or 5 or 50 unpacked, and you can move goods between horse and wagon. Calling a loaded horse to you costs part of the load.

payoff.basis: Small trade runs without a wagon, topped up from the wagon since 1.16.

unlock.basis: Any registered horse.

steps: Ask a stablemaster to load cargo onto the horse, or move goods across from your wagon (1.16).
Ride it to the post yourself: don't call a loaded horse to you.
Sell at a trading post; since 1.16 even a single good sells.

location: Stables and the seven wagon workshops.

watch: 1.16 raised the cargo lost when you retrieve a horse or wagon.
Healing at a stable can cost carried trade goods.

patches.note: Trading posts show Kliff's, Damiane's and Oongka's horse inventories

name: Wagon Cargo
trait: Bulk trade, loaded by Brice or at seven workshops
summary: A wagon is the bulk carrier. Brice loads it at camp from your bag or the camp's stock, and since 1.16 seven wagon workshops package and load goods on the road: Hernand, Demeniss, Delesyia, Pailune, Tommaso, Urdavah and Varnia. No source publishes a wagon's slot count. Losing or retrieving a wagon costs part of the load.

capacity.basis: No source publishes a slot count.

unlock.basis: Brice's Request after A Rumor in Glenbright Farm; built at the Timberturner Wainwright.

tips.text: Open the map's Trade tab before you load: it shows posts, royal posts, workshops, routes and what each post pays.
